ai_analysis.key_issue: Unauthorized felling and destruction of trees within a public park or green belt area in Aligarh, constituting illegal deforestation and loss of urban canopy cover.
ai_analysis.assigned_authority: Aligarh Municipal Corporation (AMC) - Urban Forestry & Parks Division, in coordination with the Uttar Pradesh Forest Department (if the area falls under state forest land or protected zones).
ai_analysis.legal_framework: Uttar Pradesh Forest Act, 1977; Aligarh Municipal Corporation Bye-laws regarding protection of trees and green spaces; Indian Forest Act, 1927 (if applicable to state land); Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

monitoring_roadmap.procedure: Field officers from the AMC Parks Division and local police must immediately secure the site to prevent further damage. Conduct a detailed survey to count the number of felled trees, identify species, and measure the diameter at breast height (DBH) of stumps. Photograph and video document the scene, including any machinery or debris left behind, and map the exact extent of the cleared area against the original park layout plan.

Cross-reference the location with the AMC's approved tree felling register and any existing NOCs (No Objection Certificates) from the Urban Forestry Committee. Verify if any construction permits or land acquisition orders were issued for this specific plot. Check with the UP Forest Department to confirm if the land is classified as state forest or reserved area, which would elevate the legal severity. Review CCTV footage from nearby municipal or private sources to identify the time and actors involved in the felling.

Issue an immediate stop-work order if any activity is ongoing. If unauthorized, file a case under the relevant sections of the UP Forest Act or Municipal Bye-laws against the responsible individuals or entities. Impound any sawing equipment or vehicles found at the site. Issue a show-cause notice to the property owner or contractor demanding an explanation for the violation and calculating the penalty based on the value of the trees destroyed.

Mandate the restoration of the green cover by planting an equivalent number of native species within 30 days, as per the AMC's tree replacement policy. Monitor the survival rate of new saplings for at least one monsoon season. Close the case only after the penalty is paid, the restoration is verified by a joint team of AMC and Forest Department officers, and a compliance certificate is issued.
